name: Bug Spray
description: TSA rules for flying with bug spray, insect repellent, and mosquito spray in carry-on and checked luggage.

carryOn.reason: Bug spray (aerosol insect repellent) is subject to the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule in carry-on bags. Each container must be 3.4 oz (100ml) or less and fit in your quart-sized clear bag.
conditions: Container must be 3.4 oz (100ml) or less per bottle.
Must fit in your single quart-sized clear zip-top bag with other liquids.
Aerosol sprays must have a cap or protection from accidental discharge.
DEET-based and picaridin sprays are treated as liquids/aerosols — same 3-1-1 rules apply.
exceptions: Non-aerosol pump sprays are still subject to the 3.4 oz limit.
Travel-size bug spray sticks (solid) are NOT subject to the liquids rule.

checkedBag.reason: Full-size bug spray cans are allowed in checked baggage. Consumer-grade DEET and picaridin repellents are not classified as hazardous materials in checked bags when properly packaged.
conditions: Cap must be on to prevent accidental discharge.
Maximum 18 oz (500ml) per container for aerosol sprays in checked bags.
Insecticide sprays (pest control grade) are NOT permitted — only personal insect repellents.

tsa.pageTitle: Can I bring bug spray on a plane?

airlines.name: Air France
airlines.notes: Insect repellent aerosols allowed in checked baggage. Carry-on limited to 100ml containers.

airlines.name: Emirates
airlines.notes: Bug spray and insect repellents allowed in checked baggage. Carry-on subject to 100ml liquid rule.

international.note: Some countries prohibit certain aerosol sprays. Australia restricts bringing undeclared insect repellents with agricultural-grade DEET concentrations.

travelTips: Buy a travel-size bug spray (under 3.4 oz) for carry-on, and pack a full-size can in your checked bag.
Solid bug spray sticks and wrist bands are TSA-friendly and exempt from the liquids rule.
For tropical destinations, buy bug spray at your destination to avoid carry-on restrictions.

faq.question: Can I bring bug spray on a plane in my carry-on?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in containers of 3.4 oz (100ml) or less. Bug spray is an aerosol and subject to TSA 3-1-1 liquids rules in carry-on bags. Pack a travel-size bottle and put it in your quart-sized clear liquids bag.

faq.question: Can I pack full-size bug spray in my checked bag?
faq.answer: Yes! Full-size insect repellent sprays are allowed in checked baggage. Ensure the cap is on securely to prevent accidental discharge.

faq.question: Is DEET bug spray allowed on planes?
faq.answer: Yes. DEET-based insect repellents are allowed on planes — in carry-on bags (3.4 oz or less, in liquids bag) and in checked baggage (full size). Pest-control grade sprays (not personal care) are not permitted.
